title: It was built…
summary: Visit Cairo's old Citadel and talk about its history with the passive: بُنِيَ (it was built), كُتِبَ (it was written), صُنِعَ (it was made), اُكْتُشِفَ (it was discovered) and يُقَالُ (it is said).
intro: When we don't know who did something, or it doesn't matter, Arabic doesn't add a helping word like English 'was': it changes the vowels of the verb. In the past the pattern is u–i: بَنَى (he built) becomes بُنِيَ (it was built), and كَتَبَ (he wrote) becomes كُتِبَ (it was written). In the present it is yu–a: يُقَالُ (it is said), يُسَمَّى (it is called). Guides, signs, museum labels and the news use the passive all the time: بُنِيَتِ الْقَلْعَةُ فِي الْقَرْنِ الثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ (the Citadel was built in the twelfth century).
objectives: Say when a place was built with بُنِيَ and بُنِيَتْ and a century: فِي الْقَرْنِ التَّاسِعَ عَشَرَ
Form the past passive (u–i: كُتِبَ, صُنِعَ, اُكْتُشِفَ) and the present passive (yu–a: يُقَالُ, يُسَمَّى)
Pass on a story you are not sure about with يُقَالُ إِنَّ… (it is said that…)
Describe an old building with the words for century, minaret, stone and calligraphy

realLife.title: A morning at the Citadel
realLife.story: This morning Mr Karim takes the class up to the Citadel of Salah al-Din, high above Cairo. A guide called Mrs Amal shows them the old walls and the great Mosque of Muhammad Ali with its two tall minarets. Layla wants to know who built everything and when, Daniel connects it all to the Rosetta Stone, and Sami only wants to see the famous French clock that, people say, has never worked.

sentences.ar: بُنِيَتِ الْقَلْعَةُ فِي الْقَرْنِ الثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ.
sentences.en: The Citadel was built in the twelfth century.
sentences.literal: was built the citadel in the century the twelfth
segs: was built (f; -i links to the next word)

mistakes.wrong: بَنَتِ الْقَلْعَةُ فِي الْقَرْنِ الثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ.
mistakes.right: بُنِيَتِ الْقَلْعَةُ فِي الْقَرْنِ الثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ.
mistakes.why: بَنَتْ (banat) means 'she built', but the citadel did not build anything. The passive changes the vowels to u–i: بُنِيَتْ (buniyat), 'it was built'.

sentences.ar: بُنِيَ هٰذَا الْمَسْجِدُ فِي الْقَرْنِ التَّاسِعَ عَشَرَ.
sentences.en: This mosque was built in the nineteenth century.
sentences.literal: was built this the mosque in the century the nineteenth

mistakes.wrong: بُنِيَتْ هٰذَا الْمَسْجِدُ فِي الْقَرْنِ التَّاسِعَ عَشَرَ.
mistakes.right: بُنِيَ هٰذَا الْمَسْجِدُ فِي الْقَرْنِ التَّاسِعَ عَشَرَ.
mistakes.why: مَسْجِد is masculine, so the passive verb has no -t: بُنِيَ (buniya). Use بُنِيَتْ only for feminine words such as قَلْعَة or مَدِينَة.

sentences.ar: كُتِبَتْ هٰذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتُ بِخَطٍّ عَرَبِيٍّ جَمِيلٍ.
sentences.en: These words were written in beautiful Arabic calligraphy.
sentences.literal: were written these the words with a script Arabic beautiful

mistakes.wrong: كَتَبَتْ هٰذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتُ بِخَطٍّ عَرَبِيٍّ جَمِيلٍ.
mistakes.right: كُتِبَتْ هٰذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتُ بِخَطٍّ عَرَبِيٍّ جَمِيلٍ.
mistakes.why: كَتَبَتْ (katabat) is active: 'she wrote'. For 'were written' the first letter takes u and the second takes i: كُتِبَتْ (kutibat). Words are a non-human plural, so the verb is feminine singular.

sentences.en: This clock was made in France.
sentences.literal: was made this the clock in France

mistakes.why: سَاعَة is feminine, so the passive verb takes -t: صُنِعَتْ (ṣuniʿat), just like an active verb.

sentences.ar: اُكْتُشِفَ حَجَرُ رَشِيد فِي نِهَايَةِ الْقَرْنِ الثَّامِنَ عَشَرَ.
sentences.en: The Rosetta Stone was discovered at the end of the eighteenth century.
sentences.literal: was discovered stone (of) Rashid in end (of) the century the eighteenth

mistakes.wrong: اِكْتَشَفَ حَجَرُ رَشِيد فِي نِهَايَةِ الْقَرْنِ الثَّامِنَ عَشَرَ.
mistakes.right: اُكْتُشِفَ حَجَرُ رَشِيد فِي نِهَايَةِ الْقَرْنِ الثَّامِنَ عَشَرَ.
mistakes.why: اِكْتَشَفَ (iktashafa) means that someone discovered something, so here the stone would be the discoverer. In the passive the vowels become u, u, i: اُكْتُشِفَ (uk-tu-shi-fa), 'was discovered'.

sentences.ar: يُقَالُ إِنَّ هٰذِهِ السَّاعَةَ لَمْ تَعْمَلْ أَبَدًا.
sentences.en: It is said that this clock never worked.
sentences.literal: is said that this the clock did not work ever

mistakes.wrong: يُقَالُ أَنَّ هٰذِهِ السَّاعَةَ لَمْ تَعْمَلْ أَبَدًا.
mistakes.right: يُقَالُ إِنَّ هٰذِهِ السَّاعَةَ لَمْ تَعْمَلْ أَبَدًا.
mistakes.why: Like قَالَ, the passive يُقَالُ is followed by إِنَّ (with i), not أَنَّ.

mistakes.wrong: يَقُولُ إِنَّ هٰذِهِ السَّاعَةَ لَمْ تَعْمَلْ أَبَدًا.
mistakes.right: يُقَالُ إِنَّ هٰذِهِ السَّاعَةَ لَمْ تَعْمَلْ أَبَدًا.
mistakes.why: يَقُولُ (yaqūlu) means 'he says'. 'It is said', with nobody named, is the present passive يُقَالُ (yuqālu).

dialogue.title: A visit to the Citadel
dialogue.culture: The Citadel of Salah al-Din was the home of Egypt's rulers for almost 700 years, and from its walls you can see the whole of Cairo. The clock in the courtyard of the Muhammad Ali Mosque was a gift from King Louis-Philippe of France in the 1840s; Egypt gave France the obelisk that still stands in the Place de la Concorde in Paris. When you visit a mosque, take off your shoes at the door, dress modestly (women usually cover their hair) and speak quietly, especially at prayer times.

lines.ar: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا بِكُمْ فِي قَلْعَةِ صَلَاحِ الدِّين! أَنَا أَمَل، دَلِيلَتُكُمُ الْيَوْمَ. هٰذِهِ الْقَلْعَةُ الْقَدِيمَةُ مِنْ أَشْهَرِ الْأَمَاكِنِ فِي الْقَاهِرَة.
lines.en: Welcome to the Citadel of Salah al-Din! I'm Amal, your guide today. This old citadel is one of the most famous places in Cairo.
segs: Salah (first part of the name Salah al-Din)
al-Din (second part of the name: 'of the faith')
your guide (a woman; 'your' to a group)

lines.ar: شُكْرًا يَا سَيِّدَة أَمَل. عِنْدِي سُؤَال: مَتَى بُنِيَتْ هٰذِهِ الْقَلْعَةُ، وَمَنْ بَنَاهَا؟
lines.en: Thank you, Mrs Amal. I have a question: when was this citadel built, and who built it?

lines.ar: بُنِيَتِ الْقَلْعَةُ فِي الْقَرْنِ الثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ، فِي أَيَّامِ صَلَاحِ الدِّين. وَبُنِيَتْ أَسْوَارُهَا الْعَالِيَةُ مِنَ الْحَجَرِ لِحِمَايَةِ الْمَدِينَة.
lines.en: The citadel was built in the twelfth century, in the days of Salah al-Din. Its high walls were built of stone to protect the city.
segs: (it, f) was built (-i links to the next word)
Salah (first part of the name Salah al-Din)
al-Din (second part of the name: 'of the faith')
its walls (around a city or citadel)
to protect (lit. for the protection of)

lines.ar: يَا أُسْتَاذ كَرِيم، أَعْرِفُ صَلَاحَ الدِّين مِنْ كُتُبِ التَّارِيخ. لٰكِنْ لِمَاذَا قَالَتْ «بُنِيَتِ الْقَلْعَةُ» وَلَمْ تَقُلْ «بَنَى صَلَاحُ الدِّين الْقَلْعَةَ»؟
lines.en: Mr Karim, I know Salah al-Din from history books. But why did she say 'the citadel was built' and not 'Salah al-Din built the citadel'?
segs: Salah (first part of the name Salah al-Din)
al-Din (second part of the name: 'of the faith')
(it, f) was built (-i links to the next word)
Salah (first part of the name Salah al-Din)
al-Din (second part of the name: 'of the faith')

lines.ar: سُؤَال مُمْتَاز! «بَنَى» فِعْل عَادِيّ، أَمَّا «بُنِيَ» فَهُوَ الْمَجْهُول. نَسْتَعْمِلُهُ عِنْدَمَا لَا نَعْرِفُ مَنْ عَمِلَ الشَّيْءَ، أَوْ عِنْدَمَا لَا يُهِمُّنَا ذٰلِكَ.
lines.en: Excellent question! 'Banā' is an ordinary verb, but 'buniya' is the passive. We use it when we don't know who did the thing, or when that isn't important to us.

lines.ar: وَهٰذَا الْمَسْجِدُ الْكَبِيرُ بِالْمِئْذَنَتَيْنِ الطَّوِيلَتَيْنِ؟ هَلْ بُنِيَ مَعَ الْقَلْعَةِ فِي نَفْسِ الْوَقْت؟
lines.en: And this big mosque with the two tall minarets? Was it built together with the citadel, at the same time?

lines.ar: لَا، هٰذَا مَسْجِدُ مُحَمَّد عَلِي، وَقَدْ بُنِيَ فِي الْقَرْنِ التَّاسِعَ عَشَرَ. طُولُ كُلِّ مِئْذَنَةٍ أَكْثَرُ مِنْ ثَمَانِينَ مِتْرًا.
lines.en: No, this is the Mosque of Muhammad Ali, and it was built in the nineteenth century. Each minaret is more than eighty metres tall.
segs: Ali (name; Muhammad Ali ruled Egypt in the 1800s)

lines.ar: الْجُدْرَانُ بَيْضَاءُ وَتَلْمَعُ فِي الشَّمْس. مِنْ أَيِّ حَجَرٍ بُنِيَتْ؟ هَلْ هٰذَا رُخَام؟
lines.en: The walls are white and they shine in the sun. What kind of stone were they built from? Is this marble?

lines.ar: هٰذَا لَيْسَ رُخَامًا، بَلْ مَرْمَر. غُطِّيَتِ الْجُدْرَانُ بِالْمَرْمَر، وَلِذٰلِكَ يُسَمَّى الْمَسْجِدُ أَيْضًا «مَسْجِدَ الْمَرْمَر».
lines.en: This isn't marble, it's alabaster. The walls were covered with alabaster, and that's why the mosque is also called 'the Alabaster Mosque'.
segs: (they) were covered (-i links to the next word)

lines.ar: وَأَيْنَ السَّاعَةُ الْفَرَنْسِيَّةُ الْمَشْهُورَة؟ أَبِي قَالَ لِي إِنَّهَا لَا تَعْمَلُ، وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ أَرَاهَا بِعَيْنَيَّ.
lines.en: And where is the famous French clock? My father told me that it doesn't work, and I want to see it with my own eyes.

lines.ar: هِيَ هُنَاكَ، فَوْقَ الْبُرْجِ فِي السَّاحَة. صُنِعَتْ فِي فَرَنْسَا، وَكَانَتْ هَدِيَّةً مِنْ مَلِكِ فَرَنْسَا. يُقَالُ إِنَّهَا لَمْ تَعْمَلْ أَبَدًا!
lines.en: It's over there, on top of the tower in the courtyard. It was made in France, and it was a gift from the King of France. It's said that it never worked!

lines.ar: قِصَّة غَرِيبَة! وَلِلْفَرَنْسِيِّينَ قِصَّة أُخْرَى فِي مِصْر: اُكْتُشِفَ حَجَرُ رَشِيد عَلَى يَدِ جُنُودٍ فَرَنْسِيِّينَ فِي نِهَايَةِ الْقَرْنِ الثَّامِنَ عَشَرَ.
lines.en: What a strange story! The French have another story in Egypt: the Rosetta Stone was discovered by French soldiers at the end of the eighteenth century.
segs: and the French have (lit. and to the French)

lines.ar: وَكُتِبَ عَلَى هٰذَا الْحَجَرِ نَصٌّ وَاحِدٌ بِثَلَاثِ كِتَابَاتٍ، وَبِفَضْلِهِ فَهِمَ الْعُلَمَاءُ الْكِتَابَةَ الْمِصْرِيَّةَ الْقَدِيمَة. أَيْنَ هُوَ الْآنَ؟
lines.en: And one text was written on this stone in three scripts, and thanks to it scholars understood the ancient Egyptian writing. Where is it now?

lines.ar: هُوَ الْآنَ فِي الْمَتْحَفِ الْبَرِيطَانِيِّ فِي لَنْدَن، وَيُقَالُ إِنَّهُ أَشْهَرُ حَجَرٍ فِي الْعَالَم. وَتُوجَدُ نُسْخَةٌ مِنْهُ فِي الْمَتْحَفِ الْمِصْرِيِّ هُنَا فِي الْقَاهِرَة.
lines.en: It's now in the British Museum in London, and it's said to be the most famous stone in the world. There is a copy of it in the Egyptian Museum here in Cairo.

lines.ar: وَالْآنَ نَدْخُلُ الْمَسْجِدَ لِنَرَى الْخَطَّ الْعَرَبِيَّ الْجَمِيلَ فِي الدَّاخِل. تُخْلَعُ الْأَحْذِيَةُ هُنَا عِنْدَ الْبَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكُمْ.
lines.en: And now we're going into the mosque to see the beautiful Arabic calligraphy inside. Shoes are taken off here at the door, please.

lines.ar: سَأَكْتُبُ كُلَّ هٰذِهِ الْأَفْعَالِ فِي دَفْتَرِي: بُنِيَ، صُنِعَ، كُتِبَ، اُكْتُشِفَ، يُقَالُ. هٰذَا أَحْسَنُ دَرْسٍ عَنِ الْمَجْهُولِ حَتَّى الْآنَ!
lines.en: I'll write all these verbs in my notebook: was built, was made, was written, was discovered, it is said. This is the best lesson on the passive so far!
segs: about (-i links to the next word)

reading.title: A morning at the Citadel
reading.ar: زَارَ الطُّلَّابُ صَبَاحَ الْيَوْمِ قَلْعَةَ صَلَاحِ الدِّين. بُنِيَتِ الْقَلْعَةُ فِي الْقَرْنِ الثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ، وَبُنِيَ مَسْجِدُ مُحَمَّد عَلِي فِي الْقَرْنِ التَّاسِعَ عَشَرَ، وَيُسَمَّى أَيْضًا مَسْجِدَ الْمَرْمَر. فِي السَّاحَةِ سَاعَةٌ صُنِعَتْ فِي فَرَنْسَا، وَيُقَالُ إِنَّهَا لَمْ تَعْمَلْ أَبَدًا. وَكَتَبَ دَانْيَال فِي دَفْتَرِهِ كُلَّ أَفْعَالِ الْمَجْهُول.
reading.en: This morning the students visited the Citadel of Salah al-Din. The Citadel was built in the twelfth century, and the Mosque of Muhammad Ali was built in the nineteenth century; it is also called the Alabaster Mosque. In the courtyard there is a clock that was made in France, and it is said that it never worked. And Daniel wrote all the passive verbs in his notebook.
segs: Salah (first part of the name Salah al-Din)
al-Din (second part of the name: 'of the faith')
(it, f) was built (-i links to the next word)
Ali (name; Muhammad Ali ruled Egypt in the 1800s)

quiz.prompt: When was the Citadel of Salah al-Din built?
quiz.explain: بُنِيَتِ الْقَلْعَةُ فِي الْقَرْنِ الثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ: the Mosque of Muhammad Ali inside it is much newer (nineteenth century).
The vowels u–i make a past passive: بَنَى (he built) → بُنِيَ (it was built).

quiz.prompt: Why is the Mosque of Muhammad Ali also called 'the Alabaster Mosque'?
options: Its walls were covered with alabaster
Its minarets are made of marble
A man called Alabaster built it
quiz.explain: غُطِّيَتِ الْجُدْرَانُ بِالْمَرْمَر: the walls were covered with alabaster.

quiz.prompt: What does Mrs Amal say about the clock in the courtyard?
options: It was made in France and was a gift from the King of France
It was made in Egypt for the King of France
It is a copy, and the real clock is in London
It was made in France and it works very well
quiz.explain: صُنِعَتْ فِي فَرَنْسَا، وَكَانَتْ هَدِيَّةً مِنْ مَلِكِ فَرَنْسَا, and يُقَالُ إِنَّهَا لَمْ تَعْمَلْ أَبَدًا.
yu–a in the present makes the passive: يُقَالُ. قِيلَ is the past passive, 'it was said'.

quiz.prompt: According to Mr Karim, where is the Rosetta Stone now?
options: in the British Museum in London
in the Egyptian Museum in Cairo
quiz.explain: The Egyptian Museum in Cairo has only a copy (نُسْخَة) of it.

quiz.prompt: In اُكْتُشِفَ (uk-tu-shi-fa), which letter carries a sukūn and closes the first syllable?
quiz.explain: uk-tu-shi-fa: the k has a sukūn, so the first syllable stops on it and the t follows at once.

completion: Great! You can say when a place was built, what something was made of and when it was discovered with بُنِيَ, صُنِعَ, كُتِبَ and اُكْتُشِفَ, and pass on a story with يُقَالُ إِنَّ. Tomorrow: a formal letter.
